content:
Apple TV is kicking off its fall slate this week with <strong>Mayday</strong>, a new film starring Ryan Reynolds that blends a buddy comedy with an action spy thriller. The first reviews are unanimous, calling it a big winner.

<strong>Mayday</strong> reviews praise the action, humor, and chemistry between its two leads

Apple TV is best known for its series, currently home to hits like <em>Ted Lasso</em> and sci-fi shows <em>Dark Matter</em> and <em>Silo</em>. But its movie lineup is growing too.

Beyond the 15 free classic movies just added for subscribers, Apple has several high-profile original films debuting soon, with <strong>Mayday</strong> leading the charge.

<strong>Mayday</strong> premieres on Apple TV this Friday, September 4 (watch here).

The film stars Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh, directed by John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein. The duo previously worked together on <em>Game Night</em> and <em>Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves</em>, and co-wrote <em>Horrible Bosses</em>.

The first reviews for <strong>Mayday</strong> are in, and they're almost universally positive. Here are some highlights:

  • JoBlo: "<strong>Mayday</strong> is hands down the best non-theatrical film of the year, and one of the best streaming exclusives I've seen."
  • Empire: "When you hear the words 'Ryan Reynolds in a funny action comedy,' you probably already know what to expect — slick fights, sharp dialogue, plenty of entertainment. <strong>Mayday</strong> delivers all of that and throws in a few surprises too."
  • <em>The Hollywood Reporter</em>: "This breezy, entertaining film thrives on the wonderfully contrasting comedic chemistry between its two leads, leaving you hoping for the sequel the movie hints at."

Many reviewers noted that <strong>Mayday</strong> feels like — and probably should have been — a big-screen theatrical release.

With well-crafted action, likable humor, and Ryan Reynolds at his best, this is the kind of film that in any other era would have been a summer box office smash.

Either way, Apple TV subscribers can stream it for free starting this week.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, with discounts available through the Apple One bundle.
